title: Implement pkg/testutils differential testing harness (prd001 R1-R5)
description:
deliverable_type: code

required_reading:
  - docs/specs/product-requirements/prd001-testutils.yaml (full PRD for pkg/testutils -- DiffTest struct, RunDiffTests API, normalization hooks, file-state comparison, acceptance criteria)
  - docs/ARCHITECTURE.yaml (pkg/testutils component description, design decision DD2 on differential testing)
  - go.mod (module path and Go version)

files:
  - path: pkg/testutils/difftest.go
    action: create
    note: DiffTest struct, Normalize function type, RunDiffTests entry point, comparison and divergence reporting, TimestampNormalizer, file-state comparison

requirements:
  - id: R1
    text: "Define a DiffTest struct with fields for: Name (string, used as subtest name), Args ([]string), Stdin ([]byte, nil means EOF immediately per prd001 R1.2), Env ([]string, nil means inherit test process environment per prd001 R1.3), ExitCode (int), and Normalize (a slice of normalize functions per prd001 R4.3). Define the normalize function type as func([]byte) []byte per prd001 R1.4. Include a WorkDir field (string, empty means use a per-test temp directory per prd001 R2.5). Include a FileExpectations field for utilities whose primary output is a file per prd001 R5.1."
  - id: R2
    text: "Implement RunDiffTests(t *testing.T, goBinary string, refBinary string, tests []DiffTest) that iterates the test slice and runs each DiffTest as a named subtest via t.Run (prd001 R3.6). For each test case, invoke both the Go binary and the reference binary with identical args, stdin, env, and working directory. Capture stdout, stderr, and exit code from each binary independently per prd001 R2.1-R2.2. Impose a configurable timeout on each invocation with a default of 10 seconds; fail the test with a clear timeout message if either binary exceeds it per prd001 R2.3. Produce no output during a passing test run per prd001 R2.4."
  - id: R3
    text: "Implement comparison and divergence reporting: apply the Normalize function slice in order to both binaries' stdout and stderr before comparison (prd001 R3.1). Compare normalized stdout byte-for-byte -- any difference is a test failure (prd001 R3.2). Compare normalized stderr byte-for-byte (prd001 R3.3). Compare exit codes exactly (prd001 R3.4). On divergence, report: DiffTest args, stdin content truncated to 256 bytes, reference stdout, Go stdout, reference stderr, Go stderr, and both exit codes (prd001 R3.5)."
  - id: R4
    text: "Implement normalization hook composition: the Normalize field on DiffTest is a slice of func([]byte) []byte. Each function in the slice is applied in order to the raw output bytes, producing normalized bytes for comparison. When the slice is nil or empty, no normalization is applied per prd001 R4.1, R4.3."
  - id: R5
    text: "Implement a TimestampNormalizer function matching func([]byte) []byte that replaces common strftime timestamp patterns -- syslog format ('Feb 19 12:34:56'), HH:MM:SS elapsed format, epoch with microseconds -- with a fixed placeholder string. This normalizer is used by cmd/ts differential tests to eliminate wall-clock divergence per prd001 R4.2."
  - id: R6
    text: "Implement file-state comparison for utilities whose primary output is a file (sponge, cp, mv). DiffTest.FileExpectations specifies file paths and their expected content after execution. After both binaries run, compare expected file content byte-for-byte and report divergence in the same format as stdout divergence per prd001 R5.1-R5.2."

design_decisions:
  - id: D1
    text: "The primary API is RunDiffTests(t *testing.T, goBinary string, refBinary string, tests []DiffTest) per prd001-testutils AC1. A cmd/ package defines a []DiffTest slice and calls RunDiffTests from a TestXxx function with no other setup."
  - id: D2
    text: "Normalize field on DiffTest is a slice of func([]byte) []byte applied in order per prd001-testutils R4.3. When nil or empty, no normalization is applied. This replaces a single-function design to support composition of multiple normalizers."
  - id: D3
    text: "Binary execution uses exec.CommandContext with context.WithTimeout. Default timeout is 10 seconds per prd001-testutils R2.3. The test fails with a clear timeout message rather than hanging the test run per prd001 AC5."
  - id: D4
    text: "Each DiffTest runs as a named subtest via t.Run using the DiffTest.Name field per prd001-testutils R3.6, so individual test case failures are identifiable in go test output."
  - id: D5
    text: "Primary source file is pkg/testutils/difftest.go, named after the primary exported type DiffTest per project convention (P7). The package name is testutils."

acceptance_criteria:
  - id: AC1
    text: "DiffTest struct compiles with all fields specified in prd001-testutils R1.1-R1.4: Name, Args, Stdin, Env, ExitCode, Normalize slice, WorkDir, and FileExpectations."
  - id: AC2
    text: "RunDiffTests(t, goBinary, refBinary, tests) runs each DiffTest as a named subtest. A cmd/ package can call it from a TestXxx function with no other setup per prd001 AC1."
  - id: AC3
    text: "Each subtest executes both binaries with identical args, stdin, env, and working directory, capturing stdout, stderr, and exit code independently per prd001 R2.1-R2.2."
  - id: AC4
    text: "A timeout of 10 seconds (default) fails the test with a clear timeout message if either binary exceeds it per prd001 AC5."
  - id: AC5
    text: "Normalization functions from the Normalize slice are applied in order to both outputs before byte-for-byte comparison. A passing test run produces no output per prd001 AC2."
  - id: AC6
    text: "TimestampNormalizer replaces strftime-formatted timestamps (e.g., 'Feb 19 12:34:56') with a fixed placeholder so that ts differential tests pass despite wall-clock differences per prd001 AC3."
  - id: AC7
    text: "File-state comparison checks expected file content byte-for-byte after execution and reports divergence when the Go binary writes different content than the reference binary per prd001 AC4."
  - id: AC8
    text: "All pkg/testutils code compiles with no warnings under golangci-lint per prd001 AC6."

title: cmd/cat differential tests (prd006-cat R1-R5, prd001-testutils R1-R3)
description:
deliverable_type: code

required_reading:
  - cmd/cat/main.go (existing cat implementation to understand flag handling and output behavior)
  - pkg/testutils/difftest.go (DiffTest struct, RunDiffTests API, FileExpectation)
  - pkg/testutils/normalize.go (NormalizeFunc, ComposeNormalizers, TimestampNormalizer as reference pattern)
  - cmd/ts/ts_test.go (reference for how to structure differential tests -- TestMain build pattern, baseEnv, test case layout)
  - docs/specs/product-requirements/prd006-cat.yaml (all requirements R1-R5 and acceptance criteria)
  - docs/specs/test-suites/test-rel01.1.yaml (test case definitions for cat: cat_default_passthrough through cat_missing_file)

files:
  - path: cmd/cat/cat_test.go
    action: create
    note: Differential tests for cmd/cat exercising all cat test cases from test-rel01.1.yaml

requirements:
  - id: R1
    text: "Create a TestMain function that builds the Go cat binary into a temp directory and locates the Homebrew reference binary gcat via exec.LookPath(\"gcat\"). Follow the same pattern as cmd/ts/ts_test.go TestMain. Clean up the temp directory after tests complete."
  - id: R2
    text: "Define a baseEnv variable set to []string{\"LC_ALL=C\"} per test-rel01.1.yaml preconditions. All test cases must use this environment to eliminate locale-dependent divergence."
  - id: R3
    text: "Implement test case cat_default_passthrough: no flags, file input passes through verbatim. Create a temp file with known content \"hello\\nworld\\n\", pass the file path as args. Verify stdout matches byte-for-byte with no normalization. Traces prd006-cat R1.1, R1.5."
  - id: R4
    text: "Implement test case cat_binary_passthrough: no flags, stdin contains all 256 byte values (0x00-0xFF). Verify output bytes are identical to input bytes with no normalization. Traces prd006-cat R1.4."
  - id: R5
    text: "Implement test case cat_line_numbering_n: -n flag with stdin \"alpha\\n\\nbeta\\n\". No normalization. Traces prd006-cat R2.1."
  - id: R6
    text: "Implement test case cat_line_numbering_b: -b flag with stdin \"first\\n\\n\\nsecond\\n\". No normalization. Traces prd006-cat R2.2, R2.4."
  - id: R7
    text: "Implement test case cat_squeeze_blanks: -s flag with stdin \"a\\n\\n\\n\\nb\\n\". No normalization. Traces prd006-cat R3.1."
  - id: R8
    text: "Implement test case cat_show_nonprinting: -v flag with stdin containing bytes 0x01, 0x09, 0x1b, 0x7f, 0x80, 0xff. No normalization. Verify caret and M- notation matches gcat -v. Traces prd006-cat R4.1, R4.2."

design_decisions:
  - id: D1
    text: "Follow the cmd/ts/ts_test.go pattern exactly: TestMain builds the binary, sets goBinary and refBinary package-level vars, a single TestCatDifferential function defines a []testutils.DiffTest slice and calls testutils.RunDiffTests(t, goBinary, refBinary, tests)."
  - id: D2
    text: "For test cases that require file fixtures (cat_default_passthrough, cat_multiple_files, cat_missing_file), create the fixture files inside the test function using t.TempDir() and os.WriteFile. Set the DiffTest.WorkDir to the temp directory and use relative file paths in Args."
  - id: D3
    text: "For cat_binary_passthrough, construct the 256-byte stdin slice programmatically in a loop (for i := 0; i < 256; i++ { ... }) rather than embedding a literal."
  - id: D4
    text: "The reference binary is gcat (Homebrew coreutils), not cat (macOS BSD). Use exec.LookPath(\"gcat\") to locate it. Skip tests if gcat is not found."
  - id: D5
    text: "No normalization is needed for any cat test case. Cat output is deterministic -- there are no timestamps or non-deterministic fields. All DiffTest.Normalize fields should be nil."

acceptance_criteria:
  - id: AC1
    text: "cmd/cat/cat_test.go exists and compiles without errors."
  - id: AC2
    text: "go test ./cmd/cat/... runs without build errors when goBinary builds successfully."
  - id: AC3
    text: "All 14 test cases from test-rel01.1.yaml cat section are present as DiffTest entries: cat_default_passthrough, cat_binary_passthrough, cat_line_numbering_n, cat_line_numbering_b, cat_squeeze_blanks, cat_show_nonprinting, cat_show_ends, cat_show_tabs, cat_show_all, cat_flag_e, cat_flag_t, cat_flag_u_accepted, cat_combined_ns, cat_multiple_files, cat_stdin_dash, cat_missing_file."
  - id: AC4
    text: "Each DiffTest entry has a Name matching the test case name from test-rel01.1.yaml."
  - id: AC5
    text: "Each DiffTest entry has a comment referencing the traces from test-rel01.1.yaml (e.g., '// Traces: prd006-cat R1.1, R1.5')."
  - id: AC6
    text: "File fixture test cases (cat_default_passthrough, cat_multiple_files, cat_missing_file) create fixture files in t.TempDir() and set WorkDir on the DiffTest."
  - id: AC7
    text: "The test file follows the copyright header and package declaration pattern from cmd/ts/ts_test.go."

title: Implement cmd/sponge main.go — prd007-sponge R1-R5
description:
deliverable_type: code

required_reading:
  - docs/specs/product-requirements/prd007-sponge.yaml (full PRD with R1-R5 requirements)
  - docs/specs/use-cases/rel01.1-uc003-sponge.yaml (use case flow and success criteria)
  - docs/specs/test-suites/test-rel01.1.yaml (sponge test cases for design reference)
  - cmd/cat/main.go (reference for flag parsing pattern, SIGPIPE handling, and error reporting style)
  - cmd/wc/main.go (reference for flag parsing pattern and exit code handling)
  - pkg/testutils/difftest.go (DiffTest struct shape for understanding how tests will invoke the binary)

files:
  - path: cmd/sponge/main.go
    action: create
    note: "Full sponge implementation: soak stdin, atomic write, append mode, passthrough mode"

requirements:
  - id: R1
    text: "Read all stdin before opening the output file, using a dynamically grown in-memory buffer starting at 8192 bytes and doubling on overflow. The output file must not be opened until stdin reaches EOF. Per prd007-sponge R1.1, R1.2."
  - id: R2
    text: "When the in-memory buffer exceeds a memory threshold, spill the current buffer to a temp file in the directory specified by TMPDIR (or /tmp if unset) with the name pattern 'sponge' prefix, and continue reading stdin into the temp file. Per prd007-sponge R1.3, R1.4."
  - id: R3
    text: "Register a cleanup handler that deletes the temp file if the process exits or receives SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGHUP, or SIGPIPE before the rename completes. Per prd007-sponge R1.5."
  - id: R4
    text: "When an output filename is given, write the buffered content to a temp file then atomically rename it to the output path. If rename fails (cross-device), fall back to byte-for-byte copy then delete the temp file. Preserve the existing file's mode via lstat; apply 0666 masked by umask for new files. Use lstat (not stat) to check the output path. Per prd007-sponge R2.1-R2.5."
  - id: R5
    text: "Implement append mode (-a): when the output file exists, prepend its original content before the stdin content by copying the original file into the temp file first, then appending the stdin buffer. When the output file does not exist, -a behaves as default mode. Per prd007-sponge R3.1-R3.3."
  - id: R6
    text: "Implement passthrough mode (no output filename): write the buffered stdin content to stdout after stdin is fully consumed. For large input with temp file spill, seek to beginning and copy to stdout. For small input in memory, write the buffer directly. Per prd007-sponge R4.1-R4.3."
  - id: R7
    text: "Exit 0 on success. Exit 1 with a descriptive error message to stderr on any failure (stdin read error, temp file creation/write failure, output file open failure, rename/copy failure, memory allocation failure). Clean up the temp file on all exit paths. Per prd007-sponge R5.1-R5.4."

design_decisions:
  - id: D1
    text: "Use the manual flag parsing pattern from cmd/cat/main.go: iterate over os.Args[1:], handle '-a' as append flag, treat '--' as end of flags, remaining positional args are the output filename."
  - id: D2
    text: "Use the SIGPIPE handling pattern from cmd/cat/main.go: create a buffered signal channel, call signal.Notify for SIGPIPE, and exit 0 in a goroutine."
  - id: D3
    text: "Use os.CreateTemp for temp file creation. The directory is os.Getenv('TMPDIR') with fallback to os.TempDir(). The pattern prefix is 'sponge'."
  - id: D4
    text: "Use os.Rename for atomic write. Detect cross-device failure by checking for *os.LinkError from os.Rename, then fall back to io.Copy from the temp file to a new file at the output path."
  - id: D5
    text: "Use os.Lstat (not os.Stat) to check output path existence and read file mode, per prd007-sponge R2.4. This ensures symlinks are not followed blindly."

acceptance_criteria:
  - id: AC1
    text: "cmd/sponge compiles with 'go build ./cmd/sponge/' with no errors."
  - id: AC2
    text: "seq 1 100 | go run ./cmd/sponge /tmp/sponge-test-out.txt creates a file containing lines 1 through 100."
  - id: AC3
    text: "printf 'hello' | go run ./cmd/sponge writes 'hello' to stdout (passthrough mode)."
  - id: AC4
    text: "Append mode (-a) with an existing file prepends original content before stdin content in the output file."
  - id: AC5
    text: "An existing output file with mode 0640 retains mode 0640 after sponge overwrites it."
  - id: AC6
    text: "The temp file does not persist after the process exits, whether due to success or failure."
  - id: AC7
    text: "Exit code is 1 and a descriptive message is printed to stderr when the output file path is unwritable."

title: prd005-wc R1-R6, prd001-testutils R1-R3: cmd/wc differential tests
description:
deliverable_type: code

required_reading:
  - docs/specs/product-requirements/prd005-wc.yaml (wc requirements R1-R6)
  - docs/specs/product-requirements/prd001-testutils.yaml (harness contract R1-R5)
  - docs/specs/test-suites/test-rel01.1.yaml (wc test cases: wc_default_three_lines through wc_missing_file)
  - cmd/wc/main.go (existing wc implementation to be tested)
  - cmd/cat/cat_test.go (reference pattern for differential test files)
  - pkg/testutils/difftest.go (DiffTest struct, RunDiffTests function, FileExpectation)
  - pkg/testutils/normalize.go (NormalizeFunc, TimestampNormalizer, ComposeNormalizers)

files:
  - path: cmd/wc/wc_test.go
    action: create
    note: "Differential tests for cmd/wc exercising all wc test cases from test-rel01.1.yaml"

requirements:
  - id: R1
    text: "Create cmd/wc/wc_test.go implementing differential tests for all 13 wc test cases defined in test-rel01.1.yaml: wc_default_three_lines, wc_lines_only, wc_words_only, wc_bytes_only, wc_chars_lc_c, wc_max_line_length, wc_combined_flags_order, wc_multi_file_total, wc_total_only, wc_total_never, wc_stdin_dash, wc_empty_stdin, wc_missing_file. Per prd005-wc R1-R6 and prd001-testutils R1-R3."
  - id: R2
    text: "Implement TestMain that builds the Go wc binary into a temp directory via 'go build -o <path> .' and locates the Homebrew reference binary gwc via exec.LookPath('gwc'). Follow the exact pattern from cmd/cat/cat_test.go TestMain. Per prd001-testutils R2.1 and sources.yaml (homebrew_binary: gwc)."
  - id: R3
    text: "Implement TestWcDifferential that defines a []testutils.DiffTest slice containing all 13 test cases and calls testutils.RunDiffTests(t, goBinary, refBinary, tests). Skip if goBinary or refBinary are empty. Per prd001-testutils AC1."
  - id: R4
    text: "For multi-file test cases (wc_multi_file_total, wc_total_only, wc_total_never, wc_missing_file), create fixture files in t.TempDir() and set DiffTest.WorkDir to the fixture directory. Each fixture file contains the content specified in test-rel01.1.yaml. Per prd001-testutils R2.5."
  - id: R5
    text: "Set baseEnv to []string{'LC_ALL=C'} and apply it to all test cases. Per test-rel01.1.yaml preconditions and prd005-wc R5.1."
  - id: R6
    text: "No normalization is needed for any wc test case -- wc output is deterministic integer counts. Set Normalize to nil on all DiffTest entries. Per test-rel01.1.yaml preconditions."

design_decisions:
  - id: D1
    text: "Follow the TestMain pattern from cmd/cat/cat_test.go exactly: build Go binary to os.MkdirTemp, locate reference via exec.LookPath, defer os.RemoveAll cleanup, exit via os.Exit(m.Run()). The package is 'package main' since this is a cmd/ package."
  - id: D2
    text: "Use testutils.RunDiffTests as the sole test execution mechanism. Do not write standalone unit tests -- all verification is differential per prd001-testutils AC1."
  - id: D3
    text: "For file-based tests, create separate t.TempDir() directories per fixture group to avoid cross-contamination. Write fixture files via os.WriteFile with 0644 permissions. Use the file contents exactly as specified in test-rel01.1.yaml."
  - id: D4
    text: "Reference binary is gwc (Homebrew coreutils, g-prefixed per sources.yaml). Not 'wc' which would be the macOS BSD built-in with different behavior."
  - id: D5
    text: "Each DiffTest.Name must match the test case name from test-rel01.1.yaml (e.g., 'wc_default_three_lines') for traceability. Include comments with trace IDs (e.g., 'Traces: prd005-wc R1.1, R1.2, R1.3') matching the pattern in cmd/cat/cat_test.go."

acceptance_criteria:
  - id: AC1
    text: "cmd/wc/wc_test.go exists, compiles, and contains exactly 13 DiffTest entries matching the 13 wc test cases in test-rel01.1.yaml."
  - id: AC2
    text: "TestMain builds the Go wc binary and locates gwc. If either is unavailable, tests skip gracefully via t.Skip."
  - id: AC3
    text: "All multi-file test cases (wc_multi_file_total, wc_total_only, wc_total_never, wc_missing_file) create fixture files in isolated t.TempDir() directories with the exact content specified in test-rel01.1.yaml."
  - id: AC4
    text: "Every DiffTest uses Env: baseEnv (LC_ALL=C) and Normalize: nil."
  - id: AC5
    text: "'go build ./cmd/wc/...' succeeds with no compilation errors."
  - id: AC6
    text: "'go vet ./cmd/wc/...' produces no warnings."

title: Implement cmd/ts differential tests -- prd004-ts R9, prd001-testutils R1-R3
description:
deliverable_type: code

required_reading:
  - cmd/ts/main.go (existing ts implementation to test)
  - pkg/testutils/difftest.go (RunDiffTests API, DiffTest struct, FileExpectation)
  - pkg/testutils/normalize.go (TimestampNormalizer, NormalizeFunc, ComposeNormalizers)
  - docs/specs/test-suites/test-rel01.0.yaml (all 12 test case definitions with inputs, normalization, expected outputs, and PRD traces)
  - docs/specs/product-requirements/prd004-ts.yaml (R9 differential testing requirements)
  - docs/specs/product-requirements/prd001-testutils.yaml (harness contract, AC1 usage pattern)

files:
  - path: cmd/ts/ts_test.go
    action: create
    note: "Differential tests for cmd/ts exercising all 12 test cases from test-rel01.0.yaml"

requirements:
  - id: R1
    text: |
      Set up test binary discovery in TestMain. Build the Go ts binary via
      "go build -o <tmpdir>/ts ." and store the path in a package-level variable.
      Locate the reference binary via exec.LookPath("ts") (installed via
      brew install moreutils). If either binary is unavailable, skip all tests
      with t.Skip and a descriptive message. Per prd001-testutils AC1, the test
      function defines a []DiffTest slice and calls RunDiffTests(t, goBinary,
      refBinary, tests).
  - id: R2
    text: |
      Implement wall-clock timestamp test cases from test-rel01.0.yaml:
      default_format_three_lines (stdin "line1\nline2\nline3\n", no args),
      default_format_empty_stdin (stdin "", no args),
      default_format_partial_last_line (stdin "partial" with no trailing newline, no args),
      custom_strftime_format (args ["%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S"], stdin "hello\nworld\n"),
      and subsecond_format_dotS (args ["%.S"], stdin "test\n").
      All must apply TimestampNormalizer. Per prd004-ts R1.1-R1.6, R2.1-R2.4.
  - id: R3
    text: |
      Implement elapsed-mode test cases from test-rel01.0.yaml:
      elapsed_since_start_mode (args ["-s"], stdin "a\nb\nc\n") and
      incremental_mode (args ["-i"], stdin "first\nsecond\nthird\n").
      Both must apply TimestampNormalizer for elapsed HH:MM:SS prefixes.
      Per prd004-ts R3.1-R3.2, R4.1-R4.2.
  - id: R4
    text: |
      Implement monotonic_clock_mode test case from test-rel01.0.yaml:
      args ["-m"], stdin "tick\n". Apply TimestampNormalizer.
      Per prd004-ts R5.1-R5.2.
  - id: R5
    text: |
      Implement relative-mode test cases from test-rel01.0.yaml:
      relative_mode_syslog_timestamp (args ["-r"], stdin "Jan  1 00:00:00 boot message\n",
      apply TimestampNormalizer to replace relative age string) and
      relative_mode_no_timestamp_passthrough (args ["-r"],
      stdin "no timestamp here\n", no normalization needed).
      Per prd004-ts R6.1-R6.4.
  - id: R6
    text: |
      Implement error and mutual-exclusivity test cases from test-rel01.0.yaml:
      incremental_and_elapsed_mutually_exclusive (args ["-i", "-s"], stdin "",
      expected non-zero exit, stderr contains "usage") and
      invalid_flag (args ["-z"], stdin "", expected non-zero exit,
      stderr contains "usage"). No normalization. Per prd004-ts R3.4, R7.2.
  - id: R7
    text: |
      Implement tz_environment_respected test case from test-rel01.0.yaml:
      args ["%H:%M:%S"], stdin "event\n", env includes "TZ=UTC".
      Apply TimestampNormalizer. Per prd004-ts R8.1.
  - id: R8
    text: |
      Apply TimestampNormalizer from pkg/testutils to all DiffTest entries whose
      output contains non-deterministic wall-clock or elapsed timestamps, using the
      Normalize field ([]NormalizeFunc). This is required by prd004-ts R9.1 to
      ensure differential tests pass despite wall-clock differences between the Go
      binary and the reference binary.

design_decisions:
  - id: D1
    text: |
      Per prd001-testutils AC1, the test function defines a []DiffTest slice and calls
      RunDiffTests(t, goBinary, refBinary, tests) from a standard TestXxx function.
      The DiffTest struct is imported from pkg/testutils with fields Name, Args, Stdin,
      Env, Normalize, Timeout, and WorkDir per prd001-testutils R1.1-R1.4.
  - id: D2
    text: |
      Per test-rel01.0.yaml preconditions, all test cases set LC_ALL=C in the DiffTest.Env
      field. Wall-clock tests also set a fixed TZ (e.g., TZ=America/New_York) to ensure
      consistent strftime output. The tz_environment_respected test overrides with TZ=UTC.
  - id: D3
    text: |
      Per prd001-testutils R4.2 and AC3, TimestampNormalizer replaces strftime-formatted
      timestamps with the fixed placeholder "TIMESTAMP". It is passed in the
      DiffTest.Normalize slice ([]NormalizeFunc) per prd001-testutils R4.3. For tests
      with no non-deterministic output (invalid_flag, relative_mode_no_timestamp_passthrough),
      Normalize is nil.
  - id: D4
    text: |
      Build the Go binary in TestMain using exec.Command("go", "build", "-o", path, ".")
      to avoid requiring mage build to have been run. Use os.MkdirTemp for the binary
      output directory. Store goBinary and refBinary paths in package-level variables.
      Call os.Exit(m.Run()) at the end of TestMain.
  - id: D5
    text: |
      Per prd001-testutils R3.6, each DiffTest.Name must match the test case name from
      test-rel01.0.yaml (e.g., "default_format_three_lines", "elapsed_since_start_mode")
      so individual failures are identifiable in go test output via t.Run.

acceptance_criteria:
  - id: AC1
    text: |
      go test ./cmd/ts/... passes with no failures when both ./bin/ts (or freshly built
      binary) and reference ts (brew install moreutils) are available.
  - id: AC2
    text: |
      All 12 test cases from test-rel01.0.yaml are represented as DiffTest entries:
      default_format_three_lines, default_format_empty_stdin, default_format_partial_last_line,
      custom_strftime_format, subsecond_format_dotS, elapsed_since_start_mode,
      incremental_mode, incremental_and_elapsed_mutually_exclusive, monotonic_clock_mode,
      relative_mode_syslog_timestamp, relative_mode_no_timestamp_passthrough, invalid_flag.
  - id: AC3
    text: |
      TimestampNormalizer is applied to all DiffTest entries with non-deterministic output
      (wall-clock and elapsed timestamps). Tests without timestamps (invalid_flag,
      relative_mode_no_timestamp_passthrough) have nil Normalize.
  - id: AC4
    text: |
      All DiffTest entries include LC_ALL=C in the Env field per test-rel01.0 preconditions.
  - id: AC5
    text: |
      Tests skip gracefully with t.Skip when either the Go binary cannot be built or the
      reference ts binary is not found on PATH.
  - id: AC6
    text: cmd/ts/ts_test.go compiles with no warnings under golangci-lint.

title: Implement cmd/cat concatenation and display (prd006-cat R1-R5)
description:
deliverable_type: code

required_reading:
  - docs/specs/product-requirements/prd006-cat.yaml (full PRD for cat -- all requirements R1 through R5)
  - docs/specs/test-suites/test-rel01.1.yaml (test cases this implementation must satisfy -- cat section)
  - cmd/ts/main.go (pattern reference for utility structure, manual flag parsing, SIGPIPE handling)
  - pkg/testutils/difftest.go (DiffTest struct and RunDiffTests function used by the test file)
  - docs/ARCHITECTURE.yaml (project structure, component responsibilities, naming conventions)

files:
  - path: cmd/cat/main.go
    action: create
    note: "Complete cat implementation: concatenation, line numbering (-n/-b), blank squeezing (-s), non-printing display (-v/-E/-T/-A/-e/-t/-u), error handling, SIGPIPE"

requirements:
  - id: R1
    text: "Implement default passthrough behavior per prd006-cat R1.1-R1.5: read named files in argument order or stdin when no files given, write content verbatim to stdout, treat '-' as stdin, concatenate multiple files with no separator, preserve binary data without corruption, do not add or remove newlines."
  - id: R2
    text: "Implement line numbering per prd006-cat R2.1-R2.4: -n prepends right-justified width-6 line number followed by tab to every line (numbering starts at 1, does not reset per file). -b numbers only non-blank lines (blank lines get no number and no tab). -b overrides -n when both given. A blank line is one containing only a newline character."
  - id: R3
    text: "Implement blank-line squeezing per prd006-cat R3.1-R3.3: -s suppresses repeated blank lines (first blank is kept, subsequent consecutive blanks discarded). Squeezing applies across file boundaries. -s is compatible with -n and -b -- squeezing is applied before numbering so suppressed lines do not consume line numbers."
  - id: R4
    text: "Implement non-printing display per prd006-cat R4.1-R4.9: -v shows control chars 0x00-0x1F (except 0x09 tab, 0x0A newline) as ^X, 0x7F as ^?, 0x80-0x9F as M-^X, 0xA0-0xFE as M-X, 0xFF as M-^?. -E appends '$' before each newline. -T shows tab as ^I. -A equals -vET. -e equals -vE. -t equals -vT. -u is accepted but has no effect."
  - id: R5
    text: "Implement error handling and exit codes per prd006-cat R5.1-R5.4: exit 0 when all inputs processed successfully. Exit 1 when any input file cannot be opened -- print error to stderr, continue processing remaining files. Exit 1 on stdout write error. Do not exit non-zero due to SIGPIPE."
  - id: R6
    text: "Implement flag parsing: accept -n, -b, -s, -v, -E, -T, -A, -e, -t, -u as short flags including combined forms (e.g., -vET as a single argument). Accept '--' to terminate flag parsing. Report unrecognized flags to stderr and exit non-zero."

design_decisions:
  - id: D1
    text: "Apply transformations in the order specified by prd006-cat R4.9: squeeze blanks (-s), then non-printing display (-v/-T), then end-of-line marker (-E), then line number prefix (-n/-b). This order ensures squeezing happens on raw input, non-printing conversion does not interfere with numbering, and the dollar sign appears at the visual end of line."
  - id: D2
    text: "Use the same SIGPIPE handling pattern as cmd/ts/main.go: install a goroutine-based signal handler via signal.Notify that calls os.Exit(0) on syscall.SIGPIPE, per prd006-cat R5.4."
  - id: D3
    text: "When no transformation flags are active, use io.Copy for efficient binary passthrough per prd006-cat R1.4. When any transformation flag is active (-n, -b, -s, -v, -E, -T, or their combinations), process input byte-by-byte to apply the non-printing display logic correctly."
  - id: D4
    text: "Use manual flag parsing (not the standard flag package) to support combined short flags like -vET matching GNU cat getopt behavior. Follow the same manual parsing pattern used in cmd/ts/main.go parseFlags function."

acceptance_criteria:
  - id: AC1
    text: "cmd/cat compiles with 'go build ./cmd/cat/...' with no errors."
  - id: AC2
    text: "printf 'hello\\nworld\\n' | go run ./cmd/cat produces 'hello\\nworld\\n' verbatim -- no added or removed bytes."
  - id: AC3
    text: "printf 'alpha\\n\\nbeta\\n' | go run ./cmd/cat -n produces three numbered lines: '     1\\talpha\\n     2\\t\\n     3\\tbeta\\n'."
  - id: AC4
    text: "printf 'first\\n\\n\\nsecond\\n' | go run ./cmd/cat -b produces numbered non-blank lines only: '     1\\tfirst\\n\\n\\n     2\\tsecond\\n'."
  - id: AC5
    text: "printf 'a\\n\\n\\n\\nb\\n' | go run ./cmd/cat -s produces 'a\\n\\nb\\n' -- consecutive blanks collapsed to one."
  - id: AC6
    text: "printf '\\x01\\x09\\x1b\\x7f\\x80\\xff' | go run ./cmd/cat -v produces '^A' for 0x01, literal tab for 0x09, '^[' for 0x1b, '^?' for 0x7f, 'M-^@' for 0x80, 'M-^?' for 0xff."
  - id: AC7
    text: "printf '\\x01\\thello\\n' | go run ./cmd/cat -A produces '^A^Ihello$\\n' -- combined -vET behavior."
  - id: AC8
    text: "go run ./cmd/cat nonexistent.txt realfile.txt prints error for nonexistent.txt to stderr, outputs content of realfile.txt to stdout, and exits 1."

title: Implement cmd/wc (prd005-wc R1-R6): count lines, words, and bytes
description:
deliverable_type: code

required_reading:
  - docs/specs/product-requirements/prd005-wc.yaml (full PRD for wc)
  - docs/specs/use-cases/rel01.1-uc001-wc.yaml (use case flow and success criteria)
  - docs/specs/test-suites/test-rel01.1.yaml (wc test cases for understanding expected behavior)
  - cmd/cat/main.go (reference pattern for flag parsing, SIGPIPE handling, and file processing)
  - pkg/testutils/difftest.go (DiffTest struct -- understand the test interface the test file will use)

files:
  - path: cmd/wc/main.go
    action: create
    note: "Full wc implementation: flag parsing, counting, multi-file output, exit codes"

requirements:
  - id: R1
    text: "Implement default counting behavior: when no flags are given, print line count, word count, and byte count for each input. Read from stdin when no file arguments are given. Print one line per input with counts followed by filename; omit filename for stdin. Print a 'total' line when more than one file is given. Per prd005-wc R1.1-R1.4."
  - id: R2
    text: "Implement all counting flags: -l counts newline bytes (0x0A occurrences, not logical lines); -w counts words (maximal sequences of non-whitespace per unicode.IsSpace); -c counts bytes; -m counts characters (runes, with each invalid UTF-8 byte counting as one character) and takes precedence over -c in output; -L prints the length of the longest line measured in display columns with tab expansion to next multiple of 8. When flags are combined, print counts in fixed order: lines, words, chars-or-bytes, max-line-length, regardless of flag order. Per prd005-wc R2.1-R2.6."
  - id: R3
    text: "Implement multi-file column alignment and total modes: right-align counts in columns wide enough for the largest count across all files. Support --total=auto (default: total when >1 file), --total=always (total even for one file), --total=only (only the total line, no per-file), --total=never (no total even for multiple files). The total line uses the label 'total'. Per prd005-wc R3.1-R3.3."
  - id: R4
    text: "Implement stdin and special input handling: treat '-' as a filename argument meaning stdin. Handle binary input (arbitrary byte sequences) without corruption or panic. Handle empty input producing zero counts. Support --files0-from=FILE which reads NUL-delimited filenames from FILE; when FILE is '-', filenames are read from stdin. Per prd005-wc R4.1-R4.4."
  - id: R5
    text: "Implement exit codes: exit 0 when all inputs processed successfully; exit 1 when any input file cannot be opened or read (still process and print counts for successfully read files before exiting 1); exit 1 when a write error occurs on stdout. Per prd005-wc R6.1-R6.3."
  - id: R6
    text: "Install SIGPIPE handler so wc exits cleanly (exit 0) when stdout is closed by a downstream consumer (e.g., piping to head), matching the pattern used in cmd/cat/main.go."

design_decisions:
  - id: D1
    text: "Follow the same SIGPIPE handling pattern as cmd/cat/main.go: goroutine with signal.Notify on syscall.SIGPIPE calling os.Exit(0)."
  - id: D2
    text: "Use manual flag parsing (not Go's flag package) to support combined short flags (-lwc) and GNU-style long options (--total, --files0-from), matching the flag parsing pattern in cmd/cat/main.go."
  - id: D3
    text: "For -l, count occurrences of byte 0x0A, not logical lines. A file with no trailing newline has a newline count equal to the number of 0x0A bytes. This matches wc.c:862 behavior."
  - id: D4
    text: "For -m character counting, use utf8.RuneCount for valid UTF-8. Each invalid byte counts as one character per prd005-wc R2.4. Under LC_ALL=C, -m and -c produce identical counts per prd005-wc R5.2."
  - id: D5
    text: "Dynamic column width: compute from the maximum count value across all files and the total, right-aligning all count columns to that width. This matches GNU wc's dynamic column-width behavior per prd005-wc R3.1."

acceptance_criteria:
  - id: AC1
    text: "cmd/wc/main.go compiles with 'go build ./cmd/wc/' with no errors."
  - id: AC2
    text: "printf 'foo\\nbar baz\\n' | go run ./cmd/wc produces output matching GNU gwc format: counts '2 3 12' with appropriate spacing."
  - id: AC3
    text: "Combined flags (-w -l -c) produce counts in fixed order (lines, words, bytes) regardless of flag order on the command line."
  - id: AC4
    text: "Two-file input produces per-file count lines and a 'total' line with right-aligned columns."
  - id: AC5
    text: "--total=never with two files prints no total line; --total=only prints only the total line."
  - id: AC6
    text: "Non-existent file argument prints error to stderr, exits 1, and still processes and prints counts for remaining valid files."
  - id: AC7
    text: "Empty stdin produces zero counts ('0 0 0' for default flags)."
  - id: AC8
    text: "'go vet ./cmd/wc/' passes with no diagnostics."
